subject: Human Evolution
title: Denisovan DNA in Living People
description: A short lesson to help you apply Denisovan DNA in Living People.

hook.text: Melanesians and Aboriginal Australians carry up to 5% Denisovan DNA—more than anyone carries from Neanderthals.

buildup.text: This means their ancestors interbred with Denisovans somewhere in Southeast Asia during the migration east.

discovery.text: Some Denisovan genes boosted immune function and fat metabolism—useful adaptations for island living.

twist.text: At least two distinct Denisovan populations contributed DNA—suggesting Denisovans were widespread and diverse.

climax.text: A species known from only a handful of bones left a genetic legacy in millions of living people.

punchline.text: A ghost species lives on in Pacific islanders.

quiz.question: Which modern populations carry the most Denisovan DNA?
